info.title: Heimdall Risk Intelligence API
info.description:
Heimdall is a portfolio risk-intelligence platform for measuring exposure, analyzing performance, and testing how investments respond to adverse market scenarios.

**Disclaimer.** Heimdall is an educational portfolio-analysis tool. Its calculations are estimates based on historical data and model assumptions and do not constitute financial advice or guarantee future results.

get.description: Returns successfully whenever the API process is running.
Verifies that required dependencies are reachable. Returns 503 when the database cannot be queried.

post.description: Registers a user and signs them in. Emails are stored lower-cased.
Exchanges credentials for an access token. A failed attempt returns the same error whether or not the address is registered.
Exchanges the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new refresh cookie. Reusing an already-rotated token revokes every session of that user.
Revokes the presented refresh token and clears the cookie. Idempotent: signing out twice still succeeds.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user. Requires a valid access token.

post.description: Create a portfolio owned by the authenticated user.

get.description: Returns the authenticated user's portfolios, newest first.
Returns a portfolio with its holdings. `total_cost_basis` is acquisition cost, not market value: valuation requires market data.

patch.description: Partial update. Only the fields present in the request body are changed. `base_currency` cannot be changed, because stored positions depend on it.

delete.description: Deletes the portfolio and every position it contains. Not reversible.

get.description: List every holding in a portfolio.

schema.title: Response List Positions Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Positions Get

post.description: Adds a position. A portfolio holds at most one position per asset: `on_duplicate=reject` (the default) fails with 409, while `on_duplicate=merge` adds the quantities and recomputes the weighted-average cost.

patch.description: Partial update of quantity, average cost, or purchase date. The asset cannot be changed; delete the position and add the correct one instead.

delete.description: Remove a holding from a portfolio.

post.summary: Import holdings from a CSV file
post.description: Uploads a CSV file of holdings as `multipart/form-data`. Expected header: `symbol,quantity,average_cost,purchase_date`. `purchase_date` is optional, as a column and as a value. The file is validated in full before anything is written, and the whole import runs in one transaction: a rejected file leaves the portfolio exactly as it was. Errors identify the line and column at fault. Modes: `merge` (default) combines each row with a matching holding; `replace` deletes every existing holding first; `reject` fails if any imported symbol is already held.

get.description: Searches the configured market-data source for instruments by symbol or name. Results come from the data source, not from Heimdall's own records.

Returns stored daily bars for a symbol, fetching any missing trading days from the data source first. `adjusted_close` is the series used for every return calculation. Weekends are never treated as missing data.

parameters.name: refresh

schema.description: Fetch missing trading days before answering.
schema.title: Refresh

parameters.description: Fetch missing trading days before answering.

post.summary: Refresh market data for a portfolio
post.description: Fetches any missing daily bars for every holding in the portfolio. Repeating the call is safe: ingestion is idempotent, keyed by asset, date, and source. An asset that cannot be refreshed is reported under `failures` without preventing the others from updating.

get.description: Values every holding at its newest stored price. Holdings with no stored price are listed under `unpriced_symbols` and excluded from the total and the weights, rather than being counted as zero. `data_as_of` is the newest price date actually used, which may be older than today.

post.description:
Computes performance and risk metrics over a window and stores the result with its parameters, so it can be explained and reproduced later.

A metric that cannot be computed is returned with a null value and a reason, and the run's status becomes `partial`. Missing data is never reported as zero.

Portfolio returns use **today's weights applied to historical asset returns**. That assumption is stated in the run's `notes` and on each affected metric.

get.description: Returns a portfolio's stored analysis runs, newest first.
Returns a stored run with every metric, its unit, and its assumptions.
Returns the catalogue of historical scenarios with their exact date ranges. A historical scenario replays each asset's observed return over that window against the portfolio's current holdings.

post.description: Runs one scenario against the portfolio's current holdings and stores the result with its full scenario definition. Provide exactly one of `scenario_key` (a catalogue entry) or `custom` (an explicit shock set). **Shock precedence:** a shock on a symbol overrides one on that symbol's sector, which overrides a portfolio-wide shock. Holdings with no usable price data are listed under `excluded_symbols` and left out of the estimate rather than treated as unchanged.

get.description: Returns a portfolio's stored stress tests, newest first.
Returns a stored stress test with its position-level breakdown.
Every condition the Early Warning System can evaluate, with the unit it measures and its documented default thresholds.
Returns the portfolio's alert rules, ordered by rule type.

schema.title: Response List Alert Rules Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Alert Rules Get

post.description: Creates one rule. `parameters` is validated against the rule type's own schema, and `severity_configuration` must increase with severity. A portfolio holds at most one rule per type.

Creates the documented default rule set. Idempotent: rule types that already exist are left alone unless `restore=true`, which resets every rule to its documented defaults.

Default rules are provisioned by this call, not automatically at portfolio creation, so an empty portfolio is never evaluated before it has holdings.

parameters.name: restore

schema.description: Reset every existing rule to its documented defaults, not just add missing ones.
schema.title: Restore

parameters.description: Reset every existing rule to its documented defaults, not just add missing ones.

schema.title: Response Provision Default Rules Api V1 Portfolios  Portfolio Id  Alert Rules Defaults Post

get.description: Return one alert rule.

patch.description: Partial update. Enabling, disabling, and threshold changes all go through this endpoint. The rule type cannot be changed.

delete.description: Deletes the rule and its signal history. To stop a rule from firing while keeping its history, disable it instead.

post.description:
Evaluates every enabled rule for the portfolio and reconciles its signals: new conditions create signals, persisting conditions update them, and conditions that cleared are resolved.

A rule that fails is recorded and the run continues, so one broken rule never discards the results of the others; the run's status becomes `partial`. A rule that could not be evaluated resolves nothing, because not being able to check a condition is not evidence that it cleared.

get.description: Returns the portfolio's monitoring history, newest first.

Returns Gjallarhorn Signals for one portfolio, newest first. Filter by status, severity, type, creation date, and acknowledgement state. Resolved and dismissed signals are preserved and remain queryable.

get.description: Returns one signal with its append-only lifecycle audit trail.

post.description: Records that the user has seen the signal. **Acknowledgement does not resolve it**: the condition is still present, and only the rule engine resolves a signal when its condition is no longer observed.
Hides the signal without claiming its condition has cleared. If the same condition is observed again later, a new occurrence is created.

get.description: Returns one run with its per-rule outcome, including any failures.

post.description:
Evaluates portfolios that have at least one enabled rule. Intended for a scheduler, not for users.

Requires the configured scheduler secret in `X-Cron-Secret` or as a bearer token; the comparison is constant-time. The endpoint refuses to run when no secret is configured.

**Idempotent** for one UTC evaluation period: a repeat call for the same portfolio and period returns the existing run instead of evaluating again. Work is **bounded** by `batch_size` and resumable through `cursor`, so it fits inside a serverless function's duration. A portfolio that fails is recorded and the batch continues.

The response carries operational counts only — never portfolio names, holdings, or signal content.

Generates a Heimdall Risk Report as a PDF and stores it.

The report is assembled from **stored** analysis inputs — an analysis run, recent stress tests, and recent signals — and records those identifiers in `inputs`, so the same document can be reproduced later.

Omitting `analysis_run_id` reuses the portfolio's most recent analysis, and computes one only if none exists. A failure marks the report `failed` and leaves every analysis, stress test, and signal untouched.

get.description: Returns the portfolio's generated reports, newest first.
Returns a report's status and the inputs it was built from.
Returns the rendered PDF. Only the account that generated the report can download it.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Gjallarhorn Signals identify predefined conditions in portfolio data. They are not predictions, guarantees, or recommendations to buy, sell, or hold an investment.

AlertRuleCatalogueResponse.title: AlertRuleCatalogueResponse
AlertRuleCatalogueResponse.description: Every rule type Heimdall can evaluate.

parameters.title: Parameters
parameters.description: Validated against this rule type's own schema. Unknown keys are rejected.

severity_configuration.title: Severity Configuration
severity_configuration.description: Thresholds per severity. At least one of elevated, high, critical. They must increase with severity. Omit to use the documented defaults.

cooldown_hours.title: Cooldown Hours
cooldown_hours.description: Minimum hours between external notifications for the same signal. Never affects whether the current risk state is recorded.

AlertRuleUpdateRequest.title: AlertRuleUpdateRequest
AlertRuleUpdateRequest.description: Partial update of an alert rule. The rule type cannot be changed.

start.title: Start
start.description: Inclusive start of the analysis window. Defaults to one year before the end.

end.title: End
end.description: Inclusive end of the analysis window. Defaults to today.

confidence.title: Confidence
confidence.description: Confidence level for VaR and Expected Shortfall. Defaults to 0.95.

var_method.description: Which VaR estimate to highlight. Both are always computed.

frequency.description: Return sampling frequency, which sets the annualization factor.

annual_risk_free_rate.title: Annual Risk Free Rate
annual_risk_free_rate.description: Annual risk-free rate as a decimal, for example 0.045. De-annualized geometrically before use. Defaults to 0.

benchmark_symbol.title: Benchmark Symbol
benchmark_symbol.description: Overrides the portfolio's configured benchmark for this run.

minimum_observations.title: Minimum Observations
minimum_observations.description: Minimum return observations required for tail measures. Defaults to 30.

Instrument classification.

market-data provider has described it. It is never presented as a fact.

DuplicateAssetMode.title: DuplicateAssetMode

What to do when the asset is already held in the portfolio.

* `reject` — fail with a conflict, leaving the existing position untouched.
* `merge` — combine the quantities and recompute a weighted-average cost.

ImportMode.title: ImportMode
ImportMode.description:
How an import interacts with holdings the portfolio already has.

* `merge` — combine each imported row with the matching existing position:
  quantities add and the average cost becomes the cost-weighted mean.
* `replace` — delete every existing position, then insert the file's rows.
  The portfolio ends up containing exactly what the file describes.
* `reject` — fail if any imported symbol is already held, changing nothing.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: The import mode that was applied.

rows_read.title: Rows Read
rows_read.description: Number of holdings read from the file.

positions_merged.title: Positions Merged
positions_merged.description: Existing holdings combined with a file row.

positions_removed.title: Positions Removed
positions_removed.description: Holdings deleted. Non-zero only in replace mode.

position_count.title: Position Count
position_count.description: Holdings in the portfolio after the import.

total_cost_basis.title: Total Cost Basis
total_cost_basis.description: Sum of every holding's acquisition cost. Not a market valuation.

LogoutResponse.title: LogoutResponse
LogoutResponse.description: Result of revoking the current session.

data_as_of.title: Data As Of
data_as_of.description: The as-of date the refresh targeted, in UTC.

MarketDataRefreshResponse.title: MarketDataRefreshResponse
MarketDataRefreshResponse.description: Result of refreshing every holding in a portfolio.

MetricUnit.title: MetricUnit
MetricUnit.description:
Unit of a stored metric value.

Stored explicitly so no consumer has to guess whether 0.18 means 18% or 18.

status.title: Status
status.description: evaluated, clear, skipped, or failed. A failure never hides other results.

MonitoringRuleResult.title: MonitoringRuleResult
MonitoringRuleResult.description: What one rule did during a run.

status.description: `partial` means some rules failed; results from the others are complete.

MonitoringRunSummary.title: MonitoringRunSummary
MonitoringRunSummary.description: A monitoring run without its per-rule detail, for listings.

MonitoringStatus.title: MonitoringStatus
MonitoringStatus.description:
Outcome of a monitoring run.

`partial` is a first-class outcome: one failing rule must not discard the
results of the rules that succeeded.

base_currency.title: Base Currency
base_currency.description: ISO 4217 code. Heimdall does not convert between currencies, so a portfolio accepts only assets in this currency. Supported: USD.

benchmark_symbol.title: Benchmark Symbol
benchmark_symbol.description: Optional comparison benchmark, for example SPY.

PortfolioDetailResponse.title: PortfolioDetailResponse
PortfolioDetailResponse.description: A portfolio together with its positions.

unpriced_symbols.title: Unpriced Symbols
unpriced_symbols.description: Holdings with no stored price. Excluded from value and weights.

unknown_sector_weight.title: Unknown Sector Weight
unknown_sector_weight.description: Share of value whose sector is unknown. Sector exposure is incomplete above 0.

PortfolioSummaryResponse.title: PortfolioSummaryResponse
PortfolioSummaryResponse.description:
Current valuation of a portfolio. No historical statistics.

Uses the newest stored price for each holding, which may be older than today.
`data_as_of` and `stale_symbols` say so explicitly.

PortfolioUpdateRequest.title: PortfolioUpdateRequest
PortfolioUpdateRequest.description:
Payload for a partial portfolio update.

`base_currency` is deliberately absent: changing it would invalidate every
stored position and analysis for the portfolio.

average_cost.title: Average Cost
average_cost.description: Average acquisition cost per unit, in the portfolio base currency.

on_duplicate.description: Behaviour when the portfolio already holds this asset. `reject` fails with 409; `merge` combines quantities and recomputes the weighted-average cost.

applied_return.title: Applied Return
applied_return.description: The return applied, as a decimal fraction.

return_source.title: Return Source
return_source.description: How the applied return was determined.

contribution_to_loss.title: Contribution To Loss
contribution_to_loss.description: Share of the portfolio's total loss. Null when the scenario is not a loss overall. Negative for a holding that offset part of the loss.

PositionImpactResponse.title: PositionImpactResponse
PositionImpactResponse.description: The estimated effect of a scenario on one holding.

PositionResponse.title: PositionResponse
PositionResponse.description: A holding, as returned by the API.

PositionUpdateRequest.title: PositionUpdateRequest
PositionUpdateRequest.description:
Payload for a partial position update.

The asset cannot be changed: delete the position and add the correct one, so
that history stays interpretable.

One daily observation.

`adjusted_close` is the series Heimdall uses for every return calculation.

Lifecycle of an analysis or stress-test run.

`partial` exists because one unavailable metric must not discard the others:
a run that computed most of its metrics is more useful than a failed one.

ScenarioCatalogueItem.description: One historical scenario in the catalogue.

ScenarioCatalogueResponse.description: The available historical scenarios, with shared limitations.

ScheduledMonitoringResponse.description: Operational summary of a scheduled run.

status.title: Status
status.description: The run's status, or `deduplicated` when an equivalent run already covered this period, `already_running` when one was in progress, or `failed`. Counts are always what THIS invocation did, so a repeat reports zeroes.

ScheduledPortfolioResult.title: ScheduledPortfolioResult
ScheduledPortfolioResult.description:
Per-portfolio outcome of a scheduled run.

Deliberately carries no portfolio names, holdings, or signal content: the
scheduler is not a user and must not receive portfolio detail.

target.title: Target
target.description: Symbol or sector name. Omit for a portfolio-wide shock.

value.title: Value
value.description: Relative price change as a decimal: -0.20 is a 20% fall.

ShockRequest.title: ShockRequest
ShockRequest.description: One shock in a hypothetical scenario.

ShockTargetType.title: ShockTargetType
ShockTargetType.description:
What a hypothetical shock applies to.

Precedence, most specific first: `symbol`, then `sector`, then `portfolio`.

ShockType.title: ShockType
ShockType.description:
The kind of change a shock represents.

Only `relative_price` exists. A relative price change is the only shock that
can be applied to an equity position without modelling anything Heimdall does
not model — rate curves, credit spreads, or implied volatility.

SignalEventResponse.title: SignalEventResponse
SignalEventResponse.description: One entry in a signal's append-only audit trail.

SignalSeverity.title: SignalSeverity
SignalSeverity.description:
How much attention a signal warrants.

Ordered from least to most serious. Severity is never communicated by colour
alone: every signal carries this label, an icon name, and plain-language text.

SignalStatus.title: SignalStatus
SignalStatus.description:
Where a signal is in its lifecycle.

`acknowledged` means the user has seen it — **not** that the condition has
cleared. Only the rule engine may resolve a signal.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.default: Gjallarhorn Signals identify predefined conditions in portfolio data. They are not predictions, guarantees, or recommendations to buy, sell, or hold an investment.

status.description: `partial` means some holdings were excluded for lack of data.

excluded_symbols.title: Excluded Symbols
excluded_symbols.description: Holdings with no price data for the scenario. Not counted as zero.

StressTestRunSummary.description: A stress test without its position breakdown, for listings.
